scripts.summary: Makena follows the written discovery half of the doc closely, but the doc goes blank from the pitch on, so every pitch, price, plan and close is improvised: 9 different prices on 14 calls, price before the temperature check on 13, and outcome promises on 10. The intro's recording and confidentiality lines are said on 0 of 14 calls, and there is no safety step although 7 calls include suicide, self-harm or violence disclosures. The three changes that matter most: add the crisis stop-and-check and say the recording disclosure every time; fill the pitch, delivery, investment and close with what the 3 won calls say, with a fixed list of approved payment options; hold the price until the temperature check is done.

patches.script_says: This call is recorded in the case that you end up working with Barak, in which case I'll forward my notes over to him. But if not, everything we discuss today stays between you and I.
patches.reality: The recording disclosure (C1c) and the confidentiality line (C1b) were said on 0 of 14 calls, won or not. Every call opens with her name and role and goes straight to the goal question. All 14 are recorded and transcribed. On recuD9fhc8NSBGK9z the wife was listening on another phone and nobody said so at the open. These are the calls where prospects disclosed violence, suicide attempts and sex addiction.
patches.what_works: Nothing to copy: no call does it. The won calls open with name, role and the 45-minute check (C1f, 75% of calls), which can stay.
patches.change: Make the disclosure the second thing said on every call, ask for a spoken yes, and ask who else is listening. If they say no to recording, stop the recording and carry on. Keep the rest of the doc's intro.
new_lines: Before we get into it, two quick things. This call is recorded so I can pass accurate notes to Barak if you end up working with him. If you don't, it stays with our team. Is that okay with you?
And is anyone else with you or listening in on your end, just so I know who I'm talking to?
Everything you share today is confidential. Some of it may be personal, so the more honest you can be, the better I can tell whether Barak can actually help. Sound fair?

evidence.quote: My name's Makena, by the way, I help Barack with his onboarding application process, good to meet you.
My name is Makena. I help Rock with his client application process. Good to meet you.
But I'll just be taking some notes here during our conversation.
I am a private person.

patches.section: INTRO: RAPPORT & FRAME (new branch: safety and crisis)
patches.reality: The doc has no step for a safety disclosure. The audit found 10 crisis or wellbeing disclosures (2 critical, 5 high) on 7 of 14 closer calls, 1 setter call and 2 text threads: a wife's suicide attempt and choking with jail time (rec6IqrIcBNPKz9e9), a husband who put his hands on his partner (reckX0EYFDCGQ5w0o), a grieving mother just out of inpatient care who was 'very suicidal' (recmKsZB35MoB68hY), a partner who 'doesn't want to carry on' and a first wife who died by suicide (rec1tlTKpupDVqmfF), and 'I have to choose the last option I have' (recwyYh5D2HTXy3oB). In every case the rep acknowledged it in a line and kept selling. No call asked about current safety or gave a referral. On rec6IqrIcBNPKz9e9 the reply was that Barak can definitely help; on recmKsZB35MoB68hY the next question was what would stop her booking.
patches.what_works: Nothing in the data handles this well. Won calls give no model; this is a safety rule, not a sales tactic.
patches.change: Add a 'Stop and check' branch any rep runs the moment someone mentions suicide, self-harm, wanting to not be here, or physical violence or fear in the relationship. Ask directly about now. If there is current risk or current violence, stop selling: no price, no payment, no booking on this call. Give the crisis line, tell Barak and the manager in Slack the same day, and follow up only after they confirm they are safe and supported. If it is past and they are safe and supported now, say coaching works alongside their professional care, not instead of it, and carry on.
new_lines: I want to pause there, because that matters more than anything else we talk about today. Can I ask you directly: are you having any thoughts of hurting yourself or not wanting to be here right now?
[If violence was mentioned] Is anyone in the relationship afraid of being physically hurt right now? Is everyone safe at home tonight?

[If yes, or unsure] Thank you for telling me. I'm not going to talk about the program today. Right now the most important thing is that you get support. In the US you can call or text 988 any time, day or night. If you're in danger right now, call 911. [Violence] The National Domestic Violence Hotline is 1-800-799-7233, or text START to 88788. [Outside the US] I'll text you the number for where you are.
Is there someone you can be with or call tonight? I'm going to check in with you tomorrow. Is that okay?

[If it is in the past and they are safe now] I'm really glad you're safe now. Are you working with a doctor or therapist on that side of things? Barak is a coach, not a therapist, so if you work with him it's alongside that support, not instead of it.

she'd rather not have the baby, she'd rather not be here.

patches.script_says: [INSERT BARAK'S ACTUAL FIRST COMPONENT]
patches.reality: Pillar 1 has no name or content. Reps already pitch 'find the why' on 88% of pitched calls (C13a), but the doc's link back to what the prospect said ran on only 35% (C13b).
patches.what_works: recCs5H4hJqOJtQip (won): identify why you cheat and trace it back to its emotional and developmental origins. Before that, she turned his 'I don't know why' into the reason to see Barak.
patches.change: Name Pillar 1 'Find the why' and write the content in, keeping the doc's 'not a band-aid' lines after it. Barak to confirm or rename.
new_lines: PILLAR 1: FIND THE WHY

The first thing Barak does is figure out why this happened. Not just what happened, but why: what it was giving you, or what was missing, and where that pattern started, whether that's childhood, past relationships or how you see yourself.
[Cheated-on partner] For you, that means understanding why you're stuck in (their words: checking, replaying, not trusting) so it stops running your day.

You told me (their 'I don't know why' or their doubt answer). That's exactly why this comes first, because until it's addressed you can try to move forward all you want and keep ending up in the same argument. Make sense?

patches.script_says: This is where we start actually rebuilding what was broken.
patches.reality: Pillar 2 has a placeholder title and a fill-in frame only. Reps pitch repair and rebuild on 92% of pitched calls (C13c) but use the prospect's own pain in it on 54% (C13d).
patches.what_works: Two versions on the won calls. For the partner who cheated (recCs5H4hJqOJtQip): repair the impulse, attachment and validation systems and build new ones. For the hurt partner (recGhnRsvZefXBVSx): nervous system safety, clarity, emotional boundaries and self-trust.
patches.change: Name Pillar 2 'Repair and rebuild' and give the rep both versions, then the doc's 'you mentioned (their pain)' frame.
new_lines: PILLAR 2: REPAIR AND REBUILD

[Partner who cheated] This is where Barak works on the impulse itself: the attachment and validation needs behind it, and building new ways to meet them, so cheating stops being something you reach for.

[Partner who was cheated on] This is where Barak works on getting you feeling safe in your own body again, clear on what you want, with real boundaries and trust in your own judgment, so your peace doesn't depend on what your partner does that day.
For you specifically, you mentioned (their pain). So instead of (current reality), we're working toward (their desired reality). Make sense?

evidence.quote: So, repairing the impulse, the attachment, the validation systems, and basically building new ones to make cheating very unnecessary and unattractive to you
So the program is structured around, nervous system safety, clarity, emotional boundaries, personal authority, and then self-trust.

patches.what_works: recG83GHIMQ9gNUul (won couple): Barak holds both partners accountable and it becomes clear early whether the partner is willing to do the work.
patches.change: Name Pillar 3 'Make it last', add the couples line, and keep the doc's closing question.
new_lines: PILLAR 3: MAKE IT LAST

The last piece is making sure this doesn't resurface six months from now. Barak helps you build your own internal controls and the tools to handle conflict and trust day to day, so the affair stops defining the relationship.
[Couple] He'll hear both sides, he'll challenge both of you to take accountability, and he'll help you find a middle ground that's realistic for both of you.
Does that line up with what you feel like you need?

patches.reality: With no approved plans in the doc, 9 different prices were said and 10 of 14 calls used an off-sheet number. A payment plan was offered on 13 of 14. patches.section: PITCH: HIGH-LEVEL PROMISE (scope: coaching, not therapy)

patches.what_works: recG83GHIMQ9gNUul (won) draws the line plainly: he is not a therapist who keeps you for years.
patches.change: Add a scope line for any trauma, diagnosis or medication mention: Barak is a relationship coach, and clinical care stays with their clinician.
new_lines: Just so you know exactly what this is: Barak is a relationship coach, not a therapist or a doctor. He doesn't treat trauma or mental health conditions.

addressing nervous system damage.

patches.section: OBJECTIONS: AFTER PACING (think about it, no payment on the call)

scripts.summary: Setters run the framework's discovery and the range anchor on every recorded call, but the anchor 'low-to-mid four figures' sets prospects up to be surprised by $4,500 to $5,400, and setters tell leads nothing is due upfront when the closer takes payment on the call. The framework has no branch for safety disclosures, credential questions, a partner joining, or a lead saying no, and texts filled those gaps with guilt and exact prices. The three changes that matter most: fix the price anchor and say payment happens on the call; add the safety branch; add the credentials answer and texting rules.

patches.script_says: it could be anywhere in the low-to-mid four figures. Does that sound doable?
patches.reality: Prices are $4,500 and $5,400, which are mid four figures, not low. Setters say the anchor on all 4 recorded setter calls, and prospects push for a number. One setter confirmed 'around $5,000' (acti_VPkoujbISYfJz8H8r8x3z3lYRaRIadlBmRTqf2gXICD), another said $4,000 (recbpZf1niLOSFMfR), and one text lead read 'four figures' as more than he could afford. On the closer calls, couples who heard the anchor said the real price was the first they'd heard and more than expected (rec1tlTKpupDVqmfF), or repeated it as 'low to mid thousands' (recPLMk8RaNuavRQv).
patches.what_works: Emily held the range without naming a number when pushed twice (acti_YDDW5MjfFsraQ1SJGF0gZdnJeAnNK4Epv7z5b39bFT2), but the range itself set the wrong expectation.
patches.change: Drop 'low'. Say 'mid four figures' and that it can be paid monthly. Never confirm a specific number or a payment plan; that is the closer's job.
new_lines: It depends on the level of support you decide on, but it's a mid four-figure investment for the full program, and there's a monthly option. Is that something you'd be in a position to do if it's the right fit?
[If pushed for an exact number] I'd rather not guess and be wrong. It depends on whether it's just you or both of you, and Makena will go through it exactly on the call.

decisions_for_mitch: Crisis policy: confirm the stop-and-check rule (MC-02, DM-03). Who is told, who follows up, and whether anyone with current suicidal thoughts or current violence in the relationship can be sold the couples program at all. Confirm hotline numbers to give non-US leads.
Approved payment options: is the list in MC-13 complete? Decide yes or no on deposits, bi-weekly splits, the $300 first call and half-now plans, which reps used on 5 calls.
Step-downs: confirm the first month (4 sessions) and the $500 One Call Session are approved, and that both are credited toward the 12-week program.
Setter price anchor: approve 'mid four figures with a monthly option' in place of 'low-to-mid four figures', or allow setters to name $4,500 to $5,400.
The 80% stat: confirm the source, or stop using it. If kept, couples only and framed as a track record.
Barak's credentials: provide the exact, true answer to 'is he licensed?' and stop the word 'counselor' (DM-04, DM-07).
Pillar names: Barak to confirm or rename 'Find the why', 'Repair and rebuild', 'Make it last'.
Recording: confirm the disclosure wording, whether to ask for a spoken yes, and what to do when a third party is listening.
Job title: what Makena is called to leads (Client Success Manager vs onboarding), so the DM framework and closer intro match.
